question: Basilicata, Europe’s main onshore drilling hub, is at risk of an environmental overload with a number of applications relating to 15 new fossil fuel wells (as documented by Cova Contro).

These procedures are ongoing despite the fact that the region’s Water Protection Plan has not been updated for many years (subject to the 2008 adoption, under Regional Executive Decision No 142/2024) and the landscape procedure has been at a standstill for two years, preventing the application of the SEA Directive (2001/42/EC) on cumulative impacts.

Furthermore, the downgrading of Lake Pertusillo (from A2 to A3) violates the ‘nondeterioration principle’ of the Water Directive (2000/60/EC). At the same time, the national costs of access to administrative justice are prohibitive, which is in breach of the principle of non-excessive costs (Article 9(4) of the Aarhus Convention; Article 11 of Directive 2011/92/EU).
Given that cohesion funds require compliance with enabling conditions and the ‘do no significant harm’ principle, can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Does it consider the authorisation of projects involving outdated planning and deteriorated waters to be in breach of the ‘enabling conditions’, thus blocking EU funds?
Will it launch an infringement procedure against Italy for disproportionate costs of access to administrative justice (Directive 2011/92/EU)?
What opinion will it give (under Article 19 of the EIB Statute) to prevent financing for energy projects in areas without up-to-date protection plans?
